recipe.title: Buttered Toast
recipe.description: Thick bread is toasted crisp and buttered on both faces while hot, leaving a crunchy surface and a tender middle.

ingredients.name: bread, each about 19 mm (¾ inch) thick
ingredients.substitution: Use the same number of similarly sized wheat, white or sourdough slices. Gluten-free bread may toast faster.

ingredients.name: softened salted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a spreadable dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and browning differ.

steps: Arrange {{bread}} on a rack over a baking tray. Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toast for about 6–10 minutes, turning halfway, until both faces are crisp and golden. Watch the final minutes closely.
Spread {{butter|0.5}} over one face of the warm slices. Turn them over and spread the remaining {{butter|0.5}} over the other face.
Serve two slices per person immediately. For a larger batch, toast in uncrowded batches; do not multiply the oven temperature or per-batch time.
recipe.notes: The source specified bread thickness and buttering both sides but no quantities. This adaptation sets four slices, 28 g butter and an oven method. Bread size changes the portion size. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: The English and Australian Cookery Book (1864), Edward Abbott. https://archive.org/details/b21505524 Modern adaptation by SavorShelf.

recipe.title: Mashed Potatoes
recipe.description: Steamed potatoes are mashed with warm milk and a little butter for a soft, light side dish, with optional oven browning.

ingredients.name: peeled floury potatoes, cut into 3 cm chunks
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of russet potatoes; Yukon Gold gives a denser, creamier mash.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lactose-free whole milk. Unsweetened plant milk changes the flavor.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Omit for an unsalted version; do not exchange different salts by volume.

steps: Cover {{potatoes}} with cold water and leave for 30 minutes, as in the source; then drain.

Put the potato pieces in a steamer over simmering water, keeping them above the water. Cover and steam for 20–25 minutes until a fork meets no resistance. Keep water in the lower pan as needed for steaming.
Warm {{milk}} in a small saucepan until steaming, without boiling. Transfer the tender potatoes to a warm bowl and mash by hand.
Mix {{butter}} and {{salt}} into the hot mash. Stir in half the warm milk, {{milk|0.5}}, followed by the remaining {{milk|0.5}}, until evenly combined. Avoid a blender or food processor.
Serve as six side portions. For the optional browned finish, place in a shallow oven-safe dish and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 10–15 minutes.
recipe.notes: The missing potato weight and salt amount are supplied as a modern formulation. Milk and butter are interpreted as 240 ml and 14 g. The original soak and steaming method are retained. Allow about 70 minutes without browning, or 85 with it. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Mashing technique cross-check: https://www.idahopotato.com/recipes/traditional-mashed-idaho-potatoes ; quantities and steaming method above are this source adaptation, not that recipe.

recipe.title: Scrambled Eggs
recipe.description: Eggs scrambled in butter with a small splash of milk form tender curds. The source’s generous pepper amount gives a pronounced peppery finish.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.substitution: Use pasteurized shell eggs in the same number if preferred. An egg-free replacement needs a separate formulation.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use 30 ml water for a less creamy result, or the same volume of lactose-free milk.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit to taste; salt does not provide the structure here.

ingredients.name: ground black pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use less if desired; the original recipe is strongly peppered. White pepper has a different flavor.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a dairy-free butter alternative; flavor will differ.

steps: Whisk {{eggs}}, {{milk}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}} in a bowl until evenly combined.
Melt {{butter}} in a large nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat; do not let it brown.
Pour in the egg mixture. Move a spatula slowly across the base and fold the setting curds over, cooking about 3–5 minutes until the eggs are set and no liquid egg remains.
Remove from the heat and divide into three portions. Serve immediately; the pan’s retained heat continues to firm the eggs.
recipe.notes: This adaptation keeps the six-egg formula, interprets the old milk and butter measures in metric, supplies weighed seasoning and a three-portion yield, and clarifies heat and doneness. Pan size and stove heat affect timing. Yield and timing are planning estimates. This adaptation has not been kitchen-tested.
recipe.source: Canadian Farm Cook Book (1911), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/canadianfarmcook00unse Modern adaptation by SavorShelf. Technique cross-check: https://www.incredibleegg.org/recipe/basic-scrambled-eggs/ ; this retains the historical formula rather than the reference recipe’s proportions.

recipe.title: Perunalunta (Riced Potatoes)
recipe.description: Cooked potatoes are pressed through a ricer into a light mound and seasoned with salt; this dish contains no rice.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, cut into equal 3 cm pieces
ingredients.substitution: Use a similarly sized potato with the same texture: waxy for intact pieces; floury for ricing. Large whole potatoes need longer cooking.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Use floury potatoes and rinse the cut pieces.
Place the potatoes in a saucepan with {{water}}. The water should cover them by about 1 cm; add enough cold water if the pan requires it.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently until tender to the center: about 15–20 minutes for 3 cm pieces.
Drain and let steam escape for 2–3 minutes. While hot, press through a potato ricer into a serving dish. Sprinkle evenly with {{salt}} and serve without compacting the potato.
recipe.notes: A tenderness test replaces dependence on the source’s fixed boiling time. The riced presentation is retained without adding milk or butter. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: cooking water

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Prepare {{potatoes}}. Remove sprouts and damaged or green areas; discard extensively green potatoes. Cover with separate cold rinsing water for 1 hour, then drain.
Bring {{water}} to a boil in a saucepan that holds the potatoes comfortably. Carefully add the potatoes; water should just cover them. If necessary, add enough hot water to cover.
Reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook about 20–25 minutes, until a thin knife enters the center without resistance. Do not use time alone as the test.
Drain carefully and return to the warm pan off the heat. Sprinkle with {{salt}} and gently shake. Cover and leave 5 minutes, as in the source.

recipe.title: Plain Rice to Serve with Curry
recipe.description: Basmati rice is boiled in salted water and drained for a plain, separate accompaniment to curry.

ingredients.name: dry white basmati rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

ingredients.name: cooking water
ingredients.substitution: Use drinking water; stock changes the flavor and salt level. Rinsing water is separate and is discarded.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit if preferred. Different salts can be exchanged by weight, not necessarily by spoon volume.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Bring {{water}} and {{salt}} to a boil in a saucepan. Add the drained rice and return to a gentle boil.
Cook uncovered until the grains are tender but separate, checking from 10 minutes for basmati or 12 minutes for other long-grain white rice; allow up to 20 minutes if needed.
Drain in a fine sieve. Return to the warm pan off the heat for 3 minutes so excess moisture can evaporate. Gently loosen and serve separately from the main dish.
recipe.notes: Rice type, batch size, water and salt quantities are supplied as modern choices. The source’s excess-water method is retained; rice-package timing and actual tenderness take priority over a historical fixed time. Quantities not stated by the source, equipment guidance, yield and timing are modern estimates. Not kitchen-tested.

recipe.description: White long-grain rice cooks in measured salted water and rests covered; this is a modern adaptation of the source’s boil-and-dry method.

ingredients.name: dry white basmati rice
ingredients.substitution: Use another non-parboiled white long-grain rice and follow its doneness cues. Brown, parboiled and quick-cooking rice need different timings and liquid ratios.

steps: Rinse {{rice}} in a sieve under cold drinking water until the runoff is mostly clear.
Combine the drained rice with {{water}} and {{salt}} in a small, heavy saucepan with a close-fitting lid. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to the lowest heat and cook about 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. If still firm and dry, add 15–30 ml hot water and cook a few minutes longer.
Remove from the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes, then separate the grains gently with a fork. Do not multiply cooking time when scaling; use a suitable pan.

recipe.title: Melted Butter Sauce with Milk
recipe.description: A rich butter sauce uses a little milk and water with flour to give a smooth, lightly thickened finish.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened soy milk for a dairy-free variation; flavor and thickening may differ.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

steps: Whisk {{flour}} with {{milk|0.25}} in a small saucepan until smooth.
Gradually whisk in the remaining {{milk|0.75}} and {{water}}, then add {{butter}} in small pieces.
Return to medium-low heat, whisking until the sauce gently bubbles. Lower the heat and cook 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom, until smooth and thickened. Avoid a hard boil.
Serve warm. If too thick after standing, whisk in a small splash of the recipe’s liquid to restore the intended pouring consistency.
recipe.notes: The source butter quantity is about 56 g; its dessertspoon and tablespoons are assigned modern amounts. ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative; flavor and salt content differ.

ingredients.name: all-purpose wheat flour
ingredients.substitution: Use an equal weight of a gluten-free all-purpose blend intended for sauces; texture can differ. Do not replace with an equal weight of cornstarch.

ingredients.name: cold drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Unsalted vegetable stock may replace the same volume in a savory sauce, changing its flavor.

ingredients.name: fine salt

steps: Whisk {{flour}} with {{water|0.25}} in a small saucepan until smooth.

recipe.description: An uncooked mayonnaise-style sauce emulsifies oil with egg yolks and vinegar, then finishes with a little pepper.

Mix in {{pepper}}. Serve promptly, or cover and refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or colder immediately. Prepare only what is needed for the day; this recipe is not shelf-stable.

steps: Place {{feet}} in a large pot with {{water}}, adding more water only if needed to cover. Bring to a boil, skim off surface foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cover loosely and simmer for 2–4 hours, or longer if needed, until the skin and connective tissue are very tender and pull easily from the bones. Top up with water to keep submerged.

Lift out the feet and cool only until safe to handle. Remove every bone and piece of hard gristle carefully; cut the edible soft tissue into 2 cm pieces. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve.
Return the deboned meat to a clean pan. Measure {{broth}} from the strained cooking liquid and add it to the meat. Add {{salt}}, {{pepper}} and {{lemon}}, and simmer for 5 minutes.

Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl. Gradually whisk in several spoonfuls of hot broth, then return to the pan. Stir gently until the sauce reaches 74°C (165°F), without boiling. Remove from the heat and stir in {{butter}}. Serve immediately.

recipe.description: Whole globe artichokes are cooked until tender and served with a separate smooth milk sauce for dipping the leaves and heart.

ingredients.substitution: Use four large drained canned artichoke hearts for a smaller shortcut dish; warm them separately and omit whole-artichoke preparation and boiling.

Bring {{water}} to a boil in a pot that holds the artichokes comfortably, adding more water if needed to cover. Add the artichokes and simmer, loosely covered, for 30–45 minutes, until a leaf pulls away easily and a knife enters the base without resistance.
Lift out and drain upside down. When cool enough to handle, gently open the centers and scoop out the fuzzy choke with a spoon; do not eat the fuzzy material. Keep the tender bases and leaves intact.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.

Stir {{salt}} into the sauce. Serve the warm artichokes with the sauce alongside. Pull off each leaf and scrape the tender flesh at its base with your teeth; discard the tough leaf. Eat the tender heart after the leaves.

steps: Bring {{water}} and {{boilsalt}} to a boil. Add {{cauliflower}} and simmer for 6–8 minutes until tender but holding its shape. Drain well and keep warm.
Melt {{butter}} in a separate saucepan over low heat. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Take off the heat and gradually whisk in {{milk}} until smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir until gently bubbling. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring along the bottom.
Remove the sauce from the heat and stir in {{salt}}. Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl, slowly whisk in several spoonfuls of hot sauce, then return everything to the pan.
Stir over low heat until the sauce reaches 71°C (160°F), without boiling. Arrange the florets in a mound, spoon over the hot sauce and serve immediately.
recipe.notes: Two yolks are chosen from the source two-or-three range. The missing white-sauce formula is supplied, with a controlled final heating step. steps: Cut {{apples}} into roughly 2 cm pieces. Put them in a heavy saucepan with {{water}}.

Bring just to a boil, cover and lower the heat. Simmer for 15–25 minutes, stirring frequently, until the apples collapse easily under a spoon. Add a small splash of water only if the pan begins to dry.
Mash the apples with a potato masher, or press through a sieve for a smoother sauce.
Stir {{butter}} and {{sugar}} into the hot mashed apples until melted and dissolved.
Serve warm, or transfer to shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Freeze portions for longer storage. This is not a canning recipe.
recipe.notes: Two six-apple sources have the same butter-and-sugar finish. Prepared apple weight replaces variable fruit size. recipe.title: Pommes à la Portugaise (Sugar-Baked Apples)
recipe.description: Whole cored apples bake with sugar in their centers and finish with a light dusting of powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: medium firm baking apples, about 180 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use another firm apple of similar size; sweetness and cooking time differ by variety. Avoid substituting very large apples without allowing longer cooking.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of light brown sugar for a caramel-like flavor, or reduce to taste.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar
ingredients.substitution: Use 10 g fine granulated sugar for a slightly grainier finish.

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.
Stand the apples in a snug ovenproof dish lined with baking parchment. Divide {{sugar}} among their cavities and scatter any remainder around them. Cover loosely with foil.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Remove the foil for the final 10 minutes if the fruit is still pale.
Let stand for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with {{icing}} and serve warm.
recipe.notes: The source title is retained as a historical recipe name, not an asserted Portuguese origin. An explicit four-apple batch replaces the unspecified dishful. Baking parchment and a loose cover replace the old silver-plate/camp-oven option. steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (356°F). Rinse {{apples}}. Remove the cores and seeds with an apple corer, keeping the apples whole. Make a shallow cut through the skin around the middle of each apple to help limit splitting.

Mix {{brown}}, {{cinnamon}} and {{raisins}} and divide among the cavities. Put {{cloves}} in the dish around the apples so they can be removed later. Add {{water}} and sprinkle the tops with {{sugar}}.

Bake for 30–45 minutes, checking after 25 minutes, until a small knife enters the flesh easily. Larger or firmer apples may take longer. Cover loosely with foil if the tops darken before the centers soften. Spoon the pan liquid over the fruit halfway through; some splitting is consistent with this soft preparation.
Remove all whole cloves. Transfer the apples and syrup to a shallow container, cool briefly, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
Whisk {{white}} with {{icing}} in a clean bowl until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon. Spoon a thin layer over the chilled apples.
Whip {{cream}} until soft peaks form and serve alongside immediately. Keep the glazed fruit refrigerated until serving.

recipe.title: Compota de Peras de Invierno (Vanilla Winter Pears)
recipe.description: Whole winter pears are slowly poached in vanilla syrup and served chilled.

ingredients.name: small firm winter cooking pears, about 120 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: vanilla bean, split
ingredients.substitution: Use 1 ml vanilla extract, stirred in after cooking.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Scoop out the cores and seeds from the base with a melon baller, keeping the pears whole.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{vanilla}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 1–3 hours for hard winter pears, checking after 45 minutes. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Cool briefly in a shallow container, then refrigerate within 2 hours. Chill for at least 1 hour before serving.
recipe.notes: Five pears are selected from the source count options. A measured modern syrup replaces the ambiguous 16/32-degree concentration instructions. Coloring is omitted; natural color varies. Remove the vanilla pod before serving. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern adaptation estimates, not exact historical conversions. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking time or temperature. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder; this is not a canning recipe.

recipe.description: Pear halves simmer with cloves, cinnamon and lemon, then are served with cream and reduced syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a milder dish, or use 0.1 g ground cloves per whole clove and leave in the sauce.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

ingredients.name: lemon juice
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of lime juice for a different flavor.

ingredients.name: heavy cream
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of a plant-based cream suited to the stated use.

steps: Rinse {{pears}}. Peel them. Halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.
Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan with {{cloves}}, {{cinnamon}}, {{lemon}}. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.
Cover and simmer very gently, turning and basting carefully, until a small knife enters the flesh easily: 15–30 minutes for halves. Add a little water if the pan dries before the fruit softens.
Lift out the pears. Remove any whole spices or zest strips. Simmer the liquid uncovered for 5–10 minutes until lightly syrupy, then spoon it over the fruit.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm, or cool promptly and refrigerate.
Serve with {{cream}} poured alongside.
recipe.notes: Two same-book versions are consolidated. Missing fruit, water and spice amounts are supplied. Cream is selected from the cream-or-custard option; the shorter source cake accompaniment is retained as a named serving version. recipe.description: Covered pear halves bake slowly in a fragrant sweet syrup until tender.

steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (338°F). Peel {{pears}}, halve lengthwise and scoop out all cores and seeds.
Arrange in a snug lidded ovenproof casserole. Add {{sugar}}, {{water}}, {{cloves}} and cover.

Remove whole spices and zest strips. Let stand for 5 minutes and serve with the syrup, or cool promptly and refrigerate.

recipe.title: Compota de Peras Tostadas (Roasted and Poached Pears)
recipe.description: Pears are roasted until their skins loosen, then peeled and finished in cinnamon syrup.

ingredients.name: medium firm pears, about 170 g each
ingredients.substitution: Use firm pears of similar size; dessert pears soften sooner than hard winter cooking varieties. Check tenderness rather than relying only on time.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsweetened pear juice in a fruit dish for a sweeter flavor.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Reduce for a less sweet result; this is not a shelf-stable preserve.

ingredients.name: small cinnamon stick
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp ground cinnamon per stick; leave ground spice in the sauce.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (428°F). Rinse {{pears}} and place on a rimmed metal tray. Roast for 20–30 minutes, turning once, until the skins blister and loosen; do not deliberately char the flesh.
Cool just enough to handle. Peel away the loosened skins, halve the pears and remove all cores and seeds.
Heat {{water}}, {{sugar}} and {{cinnamon}} in a saucepan until dissolved. Add the pear halves and simmer for 10–25 minutes until tender.
Lift out the pears, discard the cinnamon stick and simmer the liquid for 5–10 minutes until syrupy. Spoon over the fruit and serve.
recipe.notes: Equivalent toasted-pear methods are consolidated. A four-pear batch and measured syrup replace unclear source quantities. Controlled roasting replaces burning the skins over an open fire; the roast-then-poach sequence remains. Missing amounts, oven settings, yields and timings are explicit modern adaptation estimates, not exact historical conversions. Not kitchen-tested. recipe.description: Cooked pear halves receive a caramelized sugar finish just before serving.

Put {{water}} and {{sugar}} in a snug saucepan. Heat gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the pears in one layer, working in batches if needed.

Lift out the pears and keep warm. Measure {{reserved}} from the cooking liquid for the coating; cool and refrigerate any unused syrup separately.
Whisk {{starch}} and {{custardsugar}} into {{milk}} in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer while whisking and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.

steps: Day 1: Prepare {{pears}}, leaving the fruit whole with a cavity for filling. Dissolve {{sugar}} in {{water}} in a snug saucepan. Add the pears and simmer very gently for 20–35 minutes, turning carefully, until just tender but intact.

Transfer pears and syrup to shallow heatproof containers. Cool briefly and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Leave refrigerated overnight; never hold the fruit overnight at room temperature.
Day 2: Return fruit and syrup to the pan, heat gently to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes. Cool and refrigerate again as on day 1.
Day 3: Gently simmer fruit and syrup for another 10 minutes. Lift the pears onto a rack over a tray to drain. Measure {{reserved}} for the coating; cool and refrigerate the unused syrup separately.
Cook {{coconut}}, {{fillsugar}} and {{fillwater}} in a small pan for 3–5 minutes, stirring until a thick moist paste forms. Let cool enough to handle and spoon into the pear cavities.
Whisk {{starch}} and {{custardsugar}} into {{milk}} in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer while whisking and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat.
Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl. Slowly whisk in a little hot milk mixture, then return to the pan. Stir over low heat until the custard reaches 82°C (180°F), without boiling.
Stir {{almonds}} and the reserved syrup into the warm custard. Cook gently, stirring for 2–3 minutes, until thick enough to coat the pears; do not boil.
Heat the oven grill/broiler. Place the filled pears in a metal baking dish, coat with the almond custard and brown briefly 15–20 cm below the heat, about 2–4 minutes, watching constantly. Serve warm.

recipe.description: Carrots, chayote, peas and cheese are layered with small fried yolk pastries, then moistened with hot broth.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.substitution: For a sauce, use the same weight of a gluten-free blend labeled for sauces; pastry requires a separate tested gluten-free dough.

ingredients.name: large pasteurized egg yolks
ingredients.substitution: Use 18 g pasteurized liquid yolk per large yolk; omitting yolk changes the recipe.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of drinking water; water for dough or starch slurry should remain cold.

ingredients.name: fine salt
ingredients.substitution: Reduce or omit, especially if using salted stock.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a block-style dairy-free butter alternative.

ingredients.name: neutral vegetable oil
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of refined sunflower or rapeseed oil.

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled and trimmed
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a different carrot variety; color and sweetness will change.

ingredients.name: young chayote, peeled and seed removed
ingredients.substitution: Use 200 g zucchini; simmer only 4–6 minutes until tender.

ingredients.name: frozen green peas
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of fresh shelled peas and cook until tender.

ingredients.name: unsalted prepared beef stock
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a different flavor; check other ingredients before treating the whole recipe as vegetarian.

ingredients.name: grated mild firm cheese
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a firm dairy-free cheese that suits your needs, or omit.

ingredients.name: ground black pepper
ingredients.substitution: Use the same amount of ground white pepper, or omit.

ingredients.name: fresh parsley, finely chopped
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of cilantro for a different flavor.

steps: Mix {{flour}}, {{yolks}}, {{salt}} and softened {{butter}}. Add {{water}} a little at a time, only as needed to make a firm pliable dough. Knead for 15 minutes, cover and rest for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut {{carrot}} and {{chayote}} into 1 cm cubes. Bring {{stock}} to a simmer, add both vegetables and cook for 12–18 minutes until tender. Add {{peas}} for the final 3–5 minutes. Lift out the vegetables with a slotted spoon, keeping the broth hot.
Roll the rested dough about 2 mm thick between sheets of baking parchment and cut into small 3 cm shapes.

Put {{fryoil}} in a heavy narrow saucepan, no more than one-third full. Heat to 175°C (347°F). Fry the pastry in small batches for 2–3 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack. Do not leave hot oil unattended.
Divide half the fried pastry among heatproof serving bowls. Layer with {{cheese}}, the cooked carrot and chayote, then the remaining pastry and peas.
Bring the reserved broth back to a simmer, stir in {{pepper}} and {{parsley}}, and ladle over the layers. Serve immediately while some pastry remains crisp.
recipe.notes: The source fried pastry and layered presentation are retained. Vegetable, stock, cheese and frying amounts are supplied; oil replaces the source frying lard. The 350 ml oil is a cooking medium, not all consumed. Water is a maximum dough allowance; yolk size and flour absorption vary. Missing amounts, yields and timings are modern adaptation estimates, not recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking times. Cool leftovers promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C (40°F) or colder.
recipe.source: Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país (1922), author not recorded. https://archive.org/details/consejosprcti00lpezguate SavorShelf measured adaptation.

recipe.title: Sopa de Sustancia de Zanahoria (Carrot Essence Soup)
recipe.description: Carrots slowly simmer in broth with a little lard and sugar, producing a light strained soup poured over toast.

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled and trimmed
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a different carrot variety; color and sweetness will change.

ingredients.name: food-grade lard
ingredients.substitution: Use 30 g unsalted butter or neutral vegetable oil.

ingredients.name: unsalted prepared beef stock
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a different flavor; check other ingredients before treating the whole recipe as vegetarian.

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.substitution: Omit for a less sweet soup.

ingredients.name: plain bread
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of gluten-free bread suitable for toasting.

steps: Chop {{carrot}} finely. Heat {{lard}} in a large saucepan and sauté the carrots for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add {{stock}} and {{sugar}}. Cover loosely and simmer very gently for at least 2 hours until the carrots are falling apart. Add small splashes of water if evaporation exposes the carrots.

Strain through a fine sieve, pressing gently to extract liquid but leaving most solids behind. Reserve the carrot solids for another use. Return the strained soup to a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil; skim any foam. It should remain thin.
Toast {{bread}} until crisp, cut into pieces and divide among heatproof bowls. Pour the hot soup over the toast and serve.
recipe.notes: A smaller eight-carrot equivalent batch replaces the source 30–40 carrots. The undefined quarter of lard and broth quantity become explicit modern amounts. Straining with most pulp held back is a disclosed interpretation of the source thin carrot essence; the original wording is preserved separately. Missing amounts, yields and timings are modern adaptation estimates, not recovered historical measurements. Not kitchen-tested. Scaling changes quantities, not cooking times. recipe.description: Carrots and onions simmer with a herb bundle, then a browned butter-and-flour roux lightly thickens the strained soup.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a different carrot variety; color and sweetness will change.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of trimmed leek, rinsing away any grit.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a different flavor; check other ingredients before treating the whole recipe as vegetarian.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of fresh celery leaves.

ingredients.substitution: Use 0.25 tsp dried thyme in a tied food-safe spice bag.

ingredients.substitution: Omit if unavailable.

steps: Slice {{carrot}} and {{onion}}. Tie {{parsley}}, {{thyme}} and {{bay}} in a food-safe herb bundle or bag. Put all in a saucepan with {{stock|0.4}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}}. Simmer, partly covered, for 30–40 minutes until very soft.
Remove and discard the herb bundle. Press the vegetables and cooking liquid through a coarse sieve into a bowl.
In the emptied saucepan, melt {{butter}}, stir in {{flour}} and cook over medium-low heat for 4–6 minutes, stirring, until light golden brown. Do not let it burn.
Remove briefly from the heat and gradually whisk in the strained vegetable mixture and {{stock|0.6}}. Return to a simmer and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until smooth and lightly thickened.
While the soup finishes, cut {{bread}} into cubes, toss with {{oil}} and bake on a tray at 180°C (356°F) for 10–15 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Serve the croutons alongside.
recipe.notes: Two matching transcriptions are consolidated. The mistranslated whisk is a herb bundle. The original 2 L initial broth belongs within the 5 L total; it is not additional. recipe.description: Whole carrots are cooked in meat stock, sieved and lightly thickened with rice flour, with toast served alongside.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of a different carrot variety; color and sweetness will change.

ingredients.name: unsalted prepared beef stock
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of unsalted vegetable stock for a different flavor; check other ingredients before treating the whole recipe as vegetarian.

ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of brown rice flour; flavor and texture differ.

ingredients.name: drinking water
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of drinking water; water for dough or starch slurry should remain cold.

steps: Put {{carrot}} in a saucepan with {{stock}} and {{salt}}. Keep small carrots whole; halve very thick ones lengthwise. Cover and simmer for 40–60 minutes until very tender.

Press the vegetables and their liquid through a coarse sieve into a clean saucepan, or use an immersion blender directly in the deep pan with its head submerged. Do not seal hot soup in a countertop blender.
Mix {{riceflour}} with {{slurry}} until smooth. Whisk into the simmering soup and cook gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until the flour is cooked and the soup lightly thickened.
Toast {{bread}} until crisp and serve alongside.
recipe.notes: The source half-pint of rice flour is not treated as a reliable mass conversion: 60 g is an explicit modern thickening choice. Stock, salt and toast amounts are supplied. steps: Cut {{carrot}}, {{onion}} and {{celery}} and {{turnip}} into small pieces. Melt {{butter|0.5}} in a large saucepan and cook the vegetables with {{salt}} and {{sugar}} for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned.
Add {{stock}} and {{pepper}}, bring to a simmer and cook for 25–35 minutes until the vegetables are very soft.

Press the vegetables and their liquid through a coarse sieve into a clean saucepan, or use an immersion blender directly in the deep pan with its head submerged. Do not seal hot soup in a countertop blender.

In a separate small pan, melt {{butter|0.5}}. Stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes. Whisk in several ladlefuls of hot soup until smooth, then stir this mixture back into the main pan. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk {{yolks}} with {{cream}} in a bowl. Gradually whisk in several spoonfuls of hot soup. Reduce the soup to low heat and slowly stir the egg mixture into it.
Cook gently, stirring, until the soup reaches 71°C (160°F). Do not boil after adding the egg mixture. Serve immediately.

steps: Put {{beef}} in a large stockpot with {{carrot}} cut in chunks, quartered {{onion}}, {{scallion}}, {{parsley}} and {{cloves}} and {{bay}}. Add {{water}}. Bring slowly to a simmer, skimming foam.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 2 hours, adding water if needed to keep the meat covered. Continue until the beef is tender. Do not brown the ingredients.

Strain the broth through a fine sieve into a bowl. Reserve the cooked meat for another meal, removing any bones; cool promptly in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours. Discard the spent vegetables and whole spices.
In a clean heavy saucepan, melt {{butter}}, stir in {{flour}} and cook for 2 minutes without coloring. Add {{mushroom}} and stir over low heat for 5 minutes.

steps: Slice {{carrot}} lengthwise and quarter {{onion}}. Melt {{butter}} in a heavy saucepan and cook the vegetables gently for 5–8 minutes, stirring, without dark browning.
Add {{stock}} and {{sugar}}. Cover loosely and simmer over very low heat for 3 hours until the carrots fall apart when pressed with a spoon. Add small splashes of water to prevent drying.

Melt {{sbutter}} in a small pan. Add {{smushroom}} and cook gently for 5 minutes without browning. Stir in {{sflour}} for 2 minutes, then gradually whisk in {{sstock}}. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until smooth. Press through a fine sieve, discard the mushroom pieces and keep the sauce warm.

steps: Put {{carrot}} whole in a saucepan with {{cookstock}}. Simmer for 25–40 minutes until tender. Lift out the carrots; cool and refrigerate the cooking stock promptly for another use.

Cut the carrots into bite-sized pieces. Melt {{butter}} in a skillet, add the carrots, {{thyme}}, {{parsley}}, {{bay}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}}, and warm gently for 10 minutes, turning. Add a little water if needed to prevent catching. Remove the bay leaf.
In a separate small saucepan, melt {{sbutter}}. Stir in {{sflour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning. Gradually whisk in {{sstock}} until smooth. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add {{lemon}} and {{sparsley}} to the sauce and simmer gently for a further 10 minutes.
Whisk {{yolks}} in a bowl. Gradually whisk in a little hot sauce, then return to the pan and stir gently until the sauce reaches 71°C (160°F), without boiling. Pour over the hot carrots and serve.
recipe.notes: The exact same-book Maître d’Hôtel sauce was recovered: it uses consommé, flour, lemon, parsley and egg yolk, rather than only herb butter. steps: Cut {{carrot}} into 1 cm cubes or strips. Bring {{soakwater}} to a boil, pour over the carrots in a heatproof bowl and let stand for 5 minutes. Drain.
Bring {{water}}, {{salt}} and {{butter}} to a boil in a saucepan. Add the carrots and simmer for 10–15 minutes until tender, then drain.
In a separate small saucepan, melt {{sbutter}}. Stir in {{sflour}} and cook for 2 minutes without browning. Gradually whisk in {{sstock}} until smooth. Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring.
